text:
maria: quick idea — instead of pure percentage-based rollout, what if we require an apply quorum across control-plane destinations before promoting a config globally?
ben: define quorum? per-region majority, or X distinct edge-pools ack?
chloe: thinking per-routing-shard acks + a global health window. so config only flips when N shards report apply-success within T seconds.
dinesh: main goal is avoid split-brain where some routers start routing new variants and we see queue pressure spikes. agree quorum could help.
alexa: console UX question — how would we surface partial apply? need a progress bar + explicit "await quorum" button in rollout modal.
maria: proposal sketch: require 3 distinct availability zones (or 50% of alive shards, whichever higher) to ack within 30s. if not met, revert to previous config.
ben: implementation note: need idempotent apply path and a way to detect partial-state. add a per-instance apply-id and verify KV version after applying.
chloe: telemetry gating: only flip metric-backed SLOs after commit. we should sample 5% of requests routed to new config during quorum window to sanity-check latency and error-rate.
dinesh: for sampling, prefer deterministic hashing on request id to avoid correlated bursts. sample-rate config should be plumbed into rollout request.
alexa: console would show sampled request analytics live, like: latency p50/p95, error-rate, top endpoints impacted. need ability to pause+inspect.
ben: edge-case: what happens when quorum is never reached because some shards are healthy but slow? we should allow a manual override after a safety TTL (e.g., 10m) with audit trail.
maria: agree, add an "override after TTL" that requires two approvers in console. ops-bot: "rollout requested: cfg-2026-03-21-72 by maria. quorum target: 3 AZs, ttl: 10m."
dinesh: instrumentation: emit events: rollout.started, apply.ack (<instance>), apply.quorum_met, apply.quorum_failed, apply.override. wire those to existing rollout-trace.
ben: small proto for config apply record (pseudo):
```
apply_record: {
  id: "cfg-2026-03-21-72",
  target_shards: ["shard-a","shard-b","shard-c",...],
  acks: {"shard-a": "ok", "shard-b": "ok"},
  status: "quorum_failed"
}
```
chloe: keep events lightweight. do not use full config blob in event. store blob in config-store and reference by id.
alexa: UX question — when override happens, console should force a brief description and checkboxes for which teams were notified.
maria: follow-ups: write RFC for quota and routing interaction (how new config may change route weights), add tests that simulate slow shard ack and validate TTL+override flows.
ben: I'll spike an implementation for per-shard acking + idempotent apply scheme tomorrow.
dinesh: I'll add instrumentation hooks in rollout-trace and a chaos test that delays one AZ.
alexa: I'll mock console modal and send screens for feedback.
chloe: we should also think about metric backfills when we sample — ensure sampling flags are recorded with metrics so we can attribute.
maria: sounds good. tagging folks: @ben @chloe @dinesh @alexa — can everyone drop 1-liner on this thread before EOD? :thumbsup:
